author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: More Good News, More Falling Stocks - Barron's
text:
By Brett Arends April 30, 2018 1:04 p.m. ET The traditionally stronger half of the year for the Dow Jones Industrial Average seems to be closing out with a whimper, not a bang .
Illustration: Getty Images The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Standard & Poor’s 500 indexes were f lat and becalmed early Monday morning , despite a raft of news items that might have been expected to give them a kick. Modest rallies had quickly faded and by shortly after noon the Dow Jones was barely in positive territory and the S&P 500 was slightly in the red. Across the NYSE and the Nasdaq, falling stocks outnumbered rising ones by 2943 to 2516.
This was even though McDonald’s (MCD) crushed earnings , corporations unveiled $100 billion worth of mergers and deals , and the l atest inflation data was in line with the Fed’s 2% target . Oh, yes, and peace seems to be breaking out in Korea , and ten year Treasury yields continue to fall further away from the market-worrying 3% threshold , easing 0.01% to 2.947% by early afternoon.
The Dallas Fed said factory activity sped up this month , while the National Association of Realtors says the housing market is being held back by a shortage of homes .
Why is the market flat? The dollar continues to rise . That’s bad for exporters. And we are hours away from finding out whether the European Union, and other countries, will be exempted from new tariffs.
Apple (AAPL) rose 2% ahead of Tuesday’s earnings news despite multiple sources worrying about sales of the new $1,000 flagship iPhone X .
As Eddy Elfenbein reminds us at Crossing Wall Street, Monday marks the end of the stock market’s historic strong season. Since 1896, he calculates, the Dow has gained an average of 7.1% during the six months between the end of October and the end of April, compared to less than half a percent, on average, between May 1 and Hallowe’en. Whether or not this leads you to follow the advice and “sell and May and go away” is another matter. When I ran the numbers some years ago I found that, at the very least, the summer months often provided at least one good buying opportunity. Make of that what you will.
Midday Movers Arconic (ARNC) down 15.2% to $19.02 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The metals firm earned 34 cents a share on revenue of $3.44 billion, while analysts expected earnings of 32 cents a share on revenue of $3.34 billion. However, for the full year, it said it expects to earn between $1.17 and $1.27 a share on revenue of $13.7 billion to $14 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.49 a share on revenue of $13.54 billion.
Celgene (CELG) is down 6% to $85.76 after Morgan Stanley warned that a re-filing for multiple sclerosis drug ozanimod may take over a year.
Diamond Offshore (DO) is down 3% $18.44. The energy firm lost 16 cents a share on revenue of $295.5 million. Analysts were looking for a 19 cent per-share loss on revenue of $295.89 million.
First Energy (FE) is up 1% to $34.62 after Wells Fargo upgraded it to Buy.
Prologis (PLD) is down 3% to $64.60 on news that it's buying DCT Industrial , up 11.6% to $65.55, in an $8.4 billion stock-for-stock transaction. — Teresa Rivas
